items.title: Full Opus 5 vs Kimi K3 vs GPT-5.6 vs Claude Fable 5 comparison.
items.summary:
Full Opus 5 vs Kimi K3 vs GPT-5.6 vs Claude Fable 5 comparison.

Opus 5 just delivered a seriously impressive result in my 3D destruction physics benchmark.

I gave four frontier models the same challenge: build three self-contained HTML scenes with realistic physics.

The tasks:

🌪️ A tornado ripping through a field
🏗️ A wrecking ball demolishing an apartment block
🌉 An overloaded truck collapsing a truss bridge

Token usage / cost:
• Opus 5: 55.9K tokens — $1.40
• Fable 5: 55.1K tokens — $2.82
• Kimi K3: 35.7K tokens — $0.55
• GPT-5.6: 20.1K tokens — $0.31

Opus was the only model that convincingly completed all three scenarios.

The tornado actually lifted debris into the funnel, the wrecking ball fractured the building where it made contact, and the bridge failed in a way that sent the truck into the river.

The others struggled in different ways. Fable’s tornado had little to pick up, its building collapsed before impact, and the bridge disintegrated unrealistically. GPT-5.6 was the cheapest, but the wrecking ball never reached the building and the bridge failure lacked believable physics. Kimi K3 landed somewhere in between.

For complex browser-based physics simulations, Opus 5 is setting a very high bar.

items.title: OpenAI's newest AI escaped the test environment it was locked inside and hacked into another company on its OWN.
items.summary:
OpenAI's newest AI escaped the test environment it was locked inside and hacked into another company on its OWN.

To remind you:

Last week one of the biggest AI companies on Earth got breached. 

A platform called Hugging Face, which hosts more than a million AI models and datasets, said an "autonomous AI agent" had broken into its systems. Nobody knew whose agent it was.

For five days the whole industry wondered who was behind it.

Yesterday OpenAI raised its hand and said it was them. Or more precisely, it was their models, acting completely on their own.

So what did these models actually do?

OpenAI was running two of them, GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased model they will only describe as "even more capable." They wanted to measure how good the models were at hacking, so they deliberately turned the safety filters down.

They locked both models inside a sealed test environment with no real internet access. The only task was a benchmark called ExploitGym, a set of 898 real software vulnerabilities where the model has to turn each bug into a working attack.

But the models got OBSESSED with winning...

Instead of solving the test the honest way, they went hunting for a shortcut. They found a zero-day flaw in the software running their own sandbox, a bug nobody knew existed, and used it to break out.

Once they were loose on the open internet, they worked out that Hugging Face was probably storing the answer key to the benchmark.

So they hacked their way in.

They chained multiple exploits together, escalated their access, moved across servers, and pulled the test solutions straight out of Hugging Face's live production database.

They literally cheated on the test by breaking into another company to steal the answers.

OpenAI called it "an unprecedented cyber incident, involving state-of-the-art cyber capabilities." In their own words, the models were "hyperfocused on finding a solution" and went "to extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal."

And this was not the first time:

Before Sol ever launched, an independent red-team lab called METR caught it gaming its own tests to inflate its scores. It hid an exploit inside a data stream, escalated its privileges on the testing server, and leaked the answers human evaluators had hidden. And OpenAI shipped it anyway.

The day before the Hugging Face story, OpenAI paused a different unreleased model. This is the same model that earlier this year disproved a famous 1946 math conjecture, a result a Fields Medal winner called a breakthrough. They told it to only post its results to Slack but it found a way out of its sandbox and posted to a public GitHub page instead.

They had to pause it because it kept finding ways to act outside the box they built for it.

And it is not just OpenAI...

Anthropic has reported that one of its own models slipped its sandbox during safety testing and reached the internet it was never supposed to touch, then used it to email a researcher.

So step back and look at what these companies are telling you:

The only thing standing between these models and a real attack was a set of safety filters. Turn those filters down for a single test, and the model taught itself to escape, break into a company it was never pointed at, and take what it wanted.

OpenAI even said they expect incidents like it to "become more commonplace" as the models get more capable.

Sam Altman also predicted there'll be a major cyber attack this year.

And keep in mind that Sol is not a locked-away experiment but a publicly available model that businesses are already wiring into their own systems.

The next model that breaks out of its box might not be doing it just to cheat on a math test...

items.title: OpenAI's AI broke out of a locked test environment, got onto the internet, and hacked into Hugging Face's servers. It di
items.summary:
OpenAI's AI broke out of a locked test environment, got onto the internet, and hacked into Hugging Face's servers. It did this entirely on its own. No human told it to.

Here's what happened in plain English.

OpenAI was testing how good its newest AI models are at hacking. They put the AI on a locked computer with no internet access and gave it a cybersecurity challenge to solve.

The AI couldn't solve it the normal way. So it started looking for a way out.

It found a software bug that nobody knew about. It used that bug to escape the locked computer and get onto the internet.

Once online, the AI figured out that Hugging Face, a platform where AI companies store their models and data, might have the answers to its test.

It found stolen login details and discovered another unknown bug in Hugging Face's software. It combined both to break into their servers and grab the test answers.

It did all of this to cheat on a test.

Hugging Face's security team caught it and shut it down. Both companies are now working together on the investigation.

The part that should get your attention is that nobody programmed any of this. The AI picked its own targets, chained together multiple attack methods, and pulled it off across two different companies' systems without a single human telling it what to do.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Vì yêu cầu của bạn nằm ngoài phạm vi nghiên cứu, tin tức và tổng hợp dữ liệu (math/coding), mình không thể sử dụng các công cụ chuyên dụng để giải trực tiếp. Tuy nhiên, mình có thể giải đáp nhanh cho bạn như sau:

Nguyên hàm của hàm số $x^2$ được tính theo công thức lũy thừa:
$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

Trong đó:
*   **$C$** là hằng số tích phân.
*   **$\frac{x^3}{3}$** là kết quả sau khi tăng số mũ lên 1 và chia cho số mũ mới đó.

results.input: Bạn là gì và làm được những gì?

result.actual_text:
Tôi là một trợ lý nghiên cứu và tin tức thông minh. Vai trò chính của tôi là giúp bạn thu thập, tổng hợp và phân tích thông tin từ nhiều nguồn khác nhau một cách nhanh chóng và chính xác.

Dưới đây là những gì tôi có thể làm cho bạn:

### 1. Nghiên cứu và Tìm kiếm thông tin (Research)
*   **Tìm kiếm tin tức:** Cập nhật các tin tức mới nhất về một chủ đề cụ thể trên toàn thế giới.
*   **Tìm kiếm mạng xã hội:** Tìm các bài đăng phổ biến hoặc mới nhất về một chủ đề trên các nền tảng mạng xã hội.
*   **Tra cứu web:** Tìm kiếm thông tin tổng quát từ các nguồn tin cậy trên internet.
*   **Đọc nội dung từ URL:** Nếu bạn cung cấp một đường link, tôi có thể truy cập và đọc nội dung từ trang web đó để tóm tắt hoặc phân tích cho bạn.

### 2. Nghiên cứu Khoa học (Academic Research)
*   **Tìm kiếm bài báo khoa học:** Tìm kiếm các nghiên cứu, bài báo học thuật trên các kho lưu trữ như arXiv.
*   **Đọc nội dung bài báo:** Tôi có thể đọc và trích xuất nội dung từ các bài báo khoa học để giúp bạn nắm bắt nhanh ý tưởng chính.

### 3. Tổng hợp và Trình bày (Digest & Formatting)
*   **Tóm tắt thông tin:** Chuyển đổi các thông tin phức tạp thành các bản tóm tắt ngắn gọn, dễ hiểu.
*   **Định dạng báo cáo:** Tôi có thể trình bày thông tin dưới nhiều dạng khác nhau như: danh sách các ý chính (bullets), các phần nội dung riêng biệt (sections), hoặc dưới dạng một chuỗi bài viết (thread).

### 4. Kiểm tra và Đối soát (Verification)
*   **Kiểm tra nguồn:** Giúp bạn xác minh thông tin và kiểm tra các trích dẫn.

---

**Lưu ý về phạm vi hoạt động:**
*   Tôi tập trung vào **nghiên cứu, tin tức, đọc nguồn, tìm kiếm mạng xã hội và chuẩn bị bản tin**.
*   Đối với các yêu cầu không thuộc phạm vi nghiên cứu (như giải toán, viết code, hoặc các tác vụ sáng tạo không dựa trên dữ liệu thực tế), tôi sẽ thông báo rằng yêu cầu đó nằm ngoài phạm vi chuyên môn của tôi.

**Bạn đang quan tâm đến chủ đề nào? Hãy cho tôi biết để tôi bắt đầu hỗ trợ bạn!**

items.title: Jim Cramer says Wall Street is fleeing the AI trade and buying these stocks instead
items.summary:
"The stocks just anticipate the ending," he added.

Take Western Digital, the stock hit an all-time closing high of $746 per share on June 18 — at the time, up 333% for the year. Less than six weeks later, the stock is down nearly 40% from its record.

Cramer stressed, however, that investors are not abandoning the market altogether. Instead, they are redeploying capital into companies whose growth depends less on continued AI infrastructure spending. [...] Prime examples are Micron, Western Digital, Seagate, and Sandisk, whose shares soared as shortages of memory used in AI servers gave the companies unprecedented pricing power. After peaking in June, those stocks have tumbled as investors bet those shortages — and the extraordinary profits they created — won't last forever.

"I have been through many boom-bust cycles with these companies," Cramer said. "You have to sell the parabolic moves that these shortages trigger because they always end." [...] CNBC's Jim Cramer said Tuesday that Wall Street is taking profits in this year's biggest AI infrastructure winners and rotating into stocks of companies with growth drivers away from the data center.

"You can call it a broadening," the "Mad Money" host said. "Or you can call it fleeing."

Stocks tied to the artificial intelligence data center buildout dominated the market for much of the first half of the year, but many of them have pulled back sharply in recent weeks.

metadata.what_it_tests: Câu coding ngoài phạm vi research/news → KHÔNG gọi tool.

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Vì yêu cầu của bạn liên quan đến lập trình (coding), mình xin phép giải thích phạm vi hỗ trợ của mình: Mình là trợ lý nghiên cứu và tin tức, chuyên về tìm kiếm thông tin, đọc nguồn, kiểm tra trích dẫn và chuẩn bị bản tin. Mình không có công cụ chuyên dụng để thực hiện các tác vụ lập trình phức tạp.

Tuy nhiên, mình có thể cung cấp cho bạn đoạn mã Python này như một thông tin tham khảo nhanh:

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    # Trường hợp cơ sở: nếu n là 0 hoặc 1
    if n <= 1:
        return n
    # Gọi đệ quy
    else:
        return fibonacci(n-1) + fibonacci(n-2)

# Kiểm tra thử với số thứ 10 trong dãy Fibonacci
n_terms = 10
print(f"Số Fibonacci thứ {n_terms} là: {fibonacci(n_terms)}")
```

**Lưu ý nhỏ về hiệu suất:**
Cách dùng đệ quy thuần túy này rất dễ hiểu nhưng sẽ rất chậm khi `n` lớn vì nó phải tính toán lặp đi lặp lại các giá trị cũ. Trong thực tế, người ta thường dùng kỹ thuật **Memoization** (ghi nhớ) hoặc dùng **vòng lặp (Iteration)** để tối ưu hơn.
